description:
1. Analyzed the codx-junior-ui codebase and produced 13 design/UI-UX documents in `design/` (brand, design system, UX, assets, governance, tokens) — finding that the brand theme CSS is dead code and three competing palettes existed.
2. Built `design/playbook/index.html`, a self-contained interactive design playbook (15 sections, live specimens, dark/light toggle, copy-to-clipboard, print stylesheet) and verified it rendering in the shared browser.
3. Updated the playbook with the two `design/resources` images: the real ribbon-glyph logo now replaces the placeholder marks in §03 (glyph, lockups, colour variants via CSS mask), and the team photo was added to §02 Brand as "the one human moment."
4. Added a new §15 "Resources & official files" section registering both assets with usage rules, downloads, and a list of still-missing files (vector master, favicon, OG card).
5. Kept docs in sync (`README.md`, `logo-system.md`, `asset-guidelines.md`) and marked the logo-mark decision answered, leaving the vector rebuild as the open phase-2 blocker.

messages.content:
Analyze and generate design documentation from codx-junior-ui to Init design folder / project 
Create all design ui/ux documents to start defining a coorporative image

I'll start by orienting in the project and locating the `codx-junior-ui` sources.Evidence gathered — including a significant finding: the brand theme CSS files are **not imported** by any entry point. Let me verify that conclusion once more before writing it up, then start the documentation set.Confirmed. Now I'll build the design documentation set.Design documentation is created in `design/` (project `codx-junior-design`) — 13 documents, all derived from the actual `client/` code, not from assumptions.

## What was produced

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `design/README.md` | Index, reading order, source-of-truth map, corporate-image deliverables checklist |
| `design/00-audit/ui-audit.md` | The UI as shipped: stack, styling pipeline, 4 shells, 412 components, 11-item inconsistency table |
| `design/01-brand/brand-platform.md` | Positioning, personas, 5 personality traits (with do/don't), brand architecture, acceptance criteria |
| `design/01-brand/logo-system.md` | Current asset audit + full spec: anatomy, clear space, 4 colour variants, 3 lockups, min sizes, misuse, export checklist |
| `design/01-brand/color-system.md` | Magenta/purple ramps + neutrals in OKLCH, semantic colours, **computed contrast table**, 10% rule |
| `design/01-brand/typography.md` | Two-voice rule, 9-step scale, code typography fix, measures, truncation |
| `design/01-brand/voice-and-tone.md` | Voice, tone per context, vocabulary table, error formula, translation safety |
| `design/02-design-system/foundations.md` | Space, radius, elevation, motion, icons, **z-index ladder**, layout grids, 6-state contract |
| `design/02-design-system/components.md` | 16 component specs (states + tokens) and a prioritised 10-item backlog |
| `design/03-ux/information-architecture.md` | The app→panel/route model, app catalogue, 4 shells, 5 core flows, nav states |
| `design/03-ux/accessibility.md` | WCAG 2.2 AA checklist with current status, keyboard map, focus contract, test protocol |
| `design/04-assets/asset-guidelines.md` | Formats, naming, screenshot rules, avatars, per-channel export specs |
| `design/05-governance/design-ops.md` | Ownership, versioning, review checklist, **5-phase adoption roadmap** |
| `design/tokens/design-tokens.json` | Machine-readable tokens ready to generate `tokens.css` |

## Highest-impact findings

1. **The brand theming is dead code.** `daisy-override.css` (598 lines re-tinting 35 themes) and both `assets/themes/codx-junior-*.css` files are **not imported** by any entry point — only `main.css → base.css` loads. The app runs on stock daisyUI palettes with two `.codx-*` helpers.
2. **Three competing palettes:** `#CC0099` (live), `#CC049C` (dead CSS, 35×), `#6366F1` indigo (an old Designer profile). Documented and resolved to magenta.
3. **Contrast, quantified:** `#CC0099` text on `#1F2937` is **3.1:1** → fails AA. Pink `#FF69B4` is 5.5:1 → the correct dark-mode text colour. White on magenta is 4.8:1 (buttons OK). Purple is 1.8:1 → fill only.
4. **No vector logo exists.** The mark is raster-only (`only_icon.png`), and `src/assets/logo.svg` is **the Vue.js logo**. This is the single biggest blocker to a corporate image.
5. **z-index bug:** modal at `z-50` paints *under* the mobile nav at `z-150`; toast/z-ladder documented as a fixed scale.
6. **`isMobile` = JS breakpoint at 1024px** — tablets get the phone shell, so any layout must be verified with `isMobile` true *and* false.

I also stored these as a durable project rule so future work doesn't reintroduce the indigo/`#CC049C` drift.

## Three decisions block the next phase

1. **Logo:** glyph + wordmark, or typographic-only (magenta hyphen as the mark)? → blocks all Phase 2 asset work.
2. **Tablets (641–1024px):** keep the mobile shell, or design a compact desktop?
3. **Light theme:** supported product theme, or convenience only? (determines the QA matrix)

Phases 0–1 in `05-governance/design-ops.md` (delete dead brand CSS, fix the broken `@font-face`, generate tokens, ship two themes) are safe to start immediately — say the word and I'll implement them.

request.content:
# codx-junior — Design Documentation

Corporate image and UI/UX foundation for **codx-junior**, derived from an audit of the
shipping product (`client/` — project `codx-junior-ui`).

> **Status:** v0.1 — *baseline definition*. Everything here describes either
> (a) what the product does **today**, verified in code, or (b) a **decision
> proposal** to close a gap. Each statement is labelled so the two never get
> confused.

---

## Why this folder exists

codx-junior grew feature-first: 400+ Vue components, several parallel shells
(desktop dockview, mobile app shell, company shell, solopreneur shell) and three
different colour palettes that leaked into the codebase over time. The product
works, but it does not yet look like *one company*.

This folder is the single place where the corporate image is defined, so that:

- a new screen can be designed without inventing new colours, spacing or copy;
- a designer and a developer can agree on a spec without a meeting;
- rebrand work (logo, palette, marketing site) has a contract to break *on purpose*.

---

## How to read it

| Folder | Contents | Audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `00-audit/` | What the current UI actually is, with file-level evidence | Designers, tech leads |
| `01-brand/` | Brand platform, logo, colour, typography, voice — the *corporate image* | Everyone, marketing included |
| `02-design-system/` | Foundations (space, radius, motion, layering) and component specs | Designers, frontend |
| `03-ux/` | Information architecture, navigation model, accessibility | Designers, PMs, frontend |
| `04-assets/` | Asset production rules: formats, sizes, naming, export | Design, marketing |
| `05-governance/` | Ownership, versioning, review checklist, adoption roadmap | Leads |
| `tokens/` | `design-tokens.json` — machine-readable source for the values above | Frontend |

Reading order for a newcomer: **audit → brand platform → colour → typography →
foundations → components → IA**.

---

## Ground rules

1. **The code is the current truth; this folder is the target truth.** When they
   disagree, the documents say which one wins.
2. **No new colour, radius or spacing value without a token.** If a value is
   missing, add a token here first, then use it.
3. **Every doc is versioned with the product**, not separately. See
   `05-governance/design-ops.md`.
4. **Numbers beat adjectives.** "16px, 8px grid, 4.5:1" is a spec; "modern and
   clean" is not.

---

## Source of truth (code references used throughout)

| Concern | File |
| --- | --- |
| Design tokens (live) | `client/src/assets/base.css` (Tailwind v4 + daisyUI 5) |
| Brand helper classes | `client/src/assets/main.css` (`--codx-primary` `#cc0099`, `--codx-secondary` `#8f008f`) |
| Unused theme drafts | `client/src/assets/daisy-override.css`, `client/src/assets/themes/*.css` ⚠️ not imported — see audit |
| Theme switch + `data-theme` | `client/src/App.vue`, `client/src/store/ui.js` (`setTheme`) |
| Application registry (IA) | `client/src/config/apps.js` |
| Mobile IA (tabs + launcher) | `client/src/config/mobile.js` |
| Shells | `client/src/App.vue`, `client/src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue`, `client/src/components/mobile/MobileShell.vue` |
| Overlays & feedback | `client/src/components/Modal.vue`, `client/src/components/Toast.vue` |
| Logos / icons | `client/public/only_icon.png`, `client/public/favicon.ico` |

---

## One-paragraph summary of the brand (TL;DR)

**codx-junior** is an AI engineering companion for teams. It is calm, dense with
information and *fast to read*. Its corporate signature is a **magenta spectrum**
(`#CC0099` → `#FF69B4`) on a **deep blue-slate** canvas, with a **system UI
typeface** for the interface and a **monospace** for anything the machine said or
wrote. The visual promise is *"the machine is working; here is exactly what it is
doing, and here is where you take over."* Every design decision should make that
promise visible.

---

## Deliverables checklist (what a "corporate image" needs)

| # | Deliverable | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Brand platform (mission, positioning, personality) | ✅ this folder |
| 2 | Logo system: vector primary, monochrome, favicon, app icon, lockups | ⬜ **missing — see `01-brand/logo-system.md`** |
| 3 | Colour tokens, light + dark, contrast-verified | ✅ defined, ⬜ not yet wired into code |
| 4 | Typography system + licensed webfont decision | ✅ stack defined, ⬜ webfont pending |
| 5 | UI component library spec | ✅ core set, ⬜ long tail |
| 6 | Accessibility conformance statement | ⬜ target set in `03-ux/accessibility.md` |
| 7 | Marketing asset kit (banner, social, deck, screenshots) | ⬜ |
| 8 | Design system published as code (`tokens` → CSS variables) | ⬜ |

Track these in the kanban board attached to this project.

request.content:
# Brand Platform

The foundation every other design decision derives from. Approved values live here;
change them here first, then propagate.

**Version:** 0.1 · **Status:** proposed baseline, pending sign-off.

---

## 1. What codx-junior is

**Category:** AI engineering companion — an agentic platform that plans, writes,
reviews and ships software *with* a team, and shows its work while doing it.

**One-line positioning**

> codx-junior is the AI teammate that runs your engineering workstream — boards,
> code, containers, browsers and docs — and lets a human take over at any moment.

**Mission**

> Give every engineering team a senior teammate that never loses context.

**What it is not**

| Not this | Because |
| --- | --- |
| A chatbot | The conversation is only the input surface; the output is commits, cards, containers, deployments |
| A code autocomplete | Most value happens outside the editor: boards, reviews, infra, knowledge |
| A "no-code" tool | The primary user reads diffs and YAML for a living |
| A toy demo | Long sessions, real repositories, multi-hour runs, budget metering |

---

## 2. Who we design for

| Persona | Context | What they need from the UI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The operator** (solo dev / solopreneur) | One person, many hats, phone + laptop | Speed. One-tap access, no ceremony, status at a glance |
| **The team lead / manager** | Cross-project view, delivery questions | Aggregation, trends, blockers, "what will be late" |
| **The platform engineer** | Containers, logs, sessions | Density, precision, copy-paste, no hidden state |
| **The reviewer** | Diffs, PRs, risks | Trust signals: what changed, why, by whom, what could break |

**Shared context — design for this, not for the exception:**

- Session length **1–3+ hours**; the interface is a *workplace*, not a landing page.
- Desktop-first, **mobile-adaptive but mobile-complete** (chat, board, review on a phone).
- Screen luminance matters: dark is the default, not an aesthetic choice.
- Users are technical: they tolerate density, they do not tolerate ambiguity.

---

## 3. Brand personality

Five traits, each with a *do* and a *don't* so it is testable.

| Trait | Do | Don't |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Competent, not boastful** | Show the evidence: file, diff, log, timestamp | "Revolutionary AI superpowers" |
| **Calm under load** | Quiet surfaces, one accent, stable layout while streaming | Flashing skeletons, bouncing badges, rainbow states |
| **Precise** | Exact numbers, units, ranges, monospace for machine values | "A lot faster", "many files" |
| **Present, not chatty** | Speak when there is something to decide | Emojis in errors, mascot interruptions |
| **Transparent** | Always show *who* acted (human vs AI) and *what happens next* | Magic that hides its own steps |

**Emotional target:** *relief*. The user should feel "someone competent is on it,
and I can see everything" — not excitement, not delight, not cuteness.

---

## 4. Brand pillars → design consequences

| Pillar | Design consequence |
| --- | --- |
| **One workplace, many tools** | One shell, one nav model, one place to find an app (fix the two-model split identified in the audit) |
| **The machine shows its work** | Every AI action has a visible trace: step, tool, duration, cost |
| **Handover is a first-class state** | "Human takes over" must be visually distinct (see `02-design-system/components.md` §11) |
| **The magenta thread** | One chromatic family, used sparsely, always meaning *"this is codx-junior / this is now"* |
| **Density with air** | 8px rhythm, tight type scale, generous gutters between *regions* rather than inside them |

---

## 5. Naming & writing the name

| Context | Form |
| --- | --- |
| Product / UI / prose | **codx-junior** (lowercase, hyphen, no space) |
| Sentence start | "Codx-junior…" — avoid; prefer restructuring |
| Technical identifiers | `codx-junior`, `codx_junior`, `CODX_JUNIOR_*` |
| Short form | **codx** is acceptable in UI chrome only (`codx-` prefix), never in marketing prose |
| Never | CodxJunior, Codx Junior, CODEX junior, codex-junior |

The name is a compound of *code* + *x* + *junior*: the junior member of the team who
does the work and reports back. That is the source of the voice — see
`01-brand/voice-and-tone.md`.

---

## 6. Logo (summary)

The signature is the **`codx-` wordmark plus a single magenta glyph**. Today only a
raster mark exists; a vector logo system is **the single highest-priority brand
deliverable**. Full spec and production checklist: `01-brand/logo-system.md`.

---

## 7. Colour (summary)

A **magenta spectrum on deep blue-slate**, in two themes only.

| Role | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brand primary | `brand.magenta.600` | `#CC0099` |
| Brand deep | `brand.purple.700` | `#8F008F` |
| Brand light (on dark) | `brand.pink.400` | `#FF69B4` |
| Canvas dark | `surface.base` | `#1F2937` |
| Canvas light | `surface.base` | `#FFFFFF` |

Machine values (OKLCH) and contrast ratios: `01-brand/color-system.md`.

**The one rule:** magenta is a *thread*, not a paint bucket. ≤10% of a screen.

---

## 8. Typography (summary)

- **UI:** system UI stack (`system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", …`) — zero webfont
  cost, native feel, perfect on every OS.
- **Machine voice:** monospace, always. Anything a machine produced — a command, a
  path, a hash, a token count, a diff — is monospace.
- **Scale:** 8 steps, `12 → 36px`, body at `14–16px`.

Full spec: `01-brand/typography.md`.

---

## 9. Imagery & motion principles

- **Screenshots, not illustrations.** The product *is* the visual. When we show
  something, it is a real surface with real data.
- **No stock people, no 3D blobs, no "AI orb".** If an illustration is unavoidable,
  use geometric line work in the magenta family on the dark canvas.
- **Motion explains, never decorates.** 150–300ms, `ease`; nothing loops forever
  except an explicit "working" indicator.
- **Dark first, light supported.** Both themes are first-class, but new surfaces are
  designed on dark and checked on light.

---

## 10. Brand architecture (how the names relate)

```
codx-junior                    ← the product / company signature
├── Harness                    ← the orchestration runtime (a capability)
├── Company                    ← the organisational shell
├── Solopreneur                ← the one-person shell
├── Workspaces                 ← containerised environments
└── <Profiles>                 ← software_developer, analyst, reviewer…
```

Rules:

- Sub-brands are **capabilities of codx-junior**, never standalone brands: they do
  not get their own logo or colour, they get their own *icon* from the shared set.
- Profiles are **human-readable roles**, written lowercase-with-underscore when
  referenced as identifiers (`software_developer`) and Title Case in prose
  ("Software Developer").
- A co-branded/white-label delivery uses the codx-junior lockup plus a partner
  monochrome mark at equal optical weight — never a merged logo.

---

## 11. What "corporate image" means in practice (acceptance criteria)

The brand is coherent when, without a logo, a screenshot is recognisable as
codx-junior. Concretely:

- [ ] Two themes only; brand magenta present on every primary screen but < 10% of pixels.
- [ ] One interface typeface family + one mono family, no third.
- [ ] Every surface uses tokens from `tokens/design-tokens.json`; no inline hex.
- [ ] The vector logo, favicon, app icon and OG image all exist and match.
- [ ] All UI copy follows `voice-and-tone.md` (reviewed in the PR template).
- [ ] A designer can produce a new screen using only this folder.

request.content: # Logo System **Status:** ⚠️ **gap.** The brand currently has no vector logo and no formal lockup. This document defines what must be produced, how it is used, and what is forbidden — so the asset work can be commissioned without further decisions. --- ## 1. Current state (audited) | Asset | Path | Format | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | App icon / avatar / favicon source | `client/public/only_icon.png` | PNG | Used by `index.html` (`rel="icon"`), `Logo.vue`, `CodxJuniorLogo.vue`, sidebar rail, `content="only_icon.png"` in docs | | Alternate mark | `client/public/demo_icon.png` | PNG | Not referenced by the app entry point | | Favicon | `client/public/favicon.ico` | ICO | Present | | Second icon copy | `client/public/public/icon.png` | PNG | Legacy nested folder | | "Brand" svg | `client/src/assets/logo.svg` | SVG | ❌ **is the Vue.js logo** (`#41b883` / `#34495e`) — scaffolding leftover | | Wordmark | rendered as HTML text | — | `DesktopSidebar.vue`: `codx-junior` | | Marketing imagery | `docs/public/images/NOV2025/*.png` (banner, avatars, screenshots) | PNG | Raster only | **Verdict:** the mark is a single raster file. There is no monochrome version, no horizontal lockup, no clear-space rule, no minimum size, no dark/light variant, and no source file. Any new surface (deck, README badge, marketplace listing, favicon at 16px) is currently a guess. --- ## 2. The mark — what it must express 1. **`codx-` is the signature.** The prefix is short, technical, and already lives in the UI chrome. The logo must read `codx` before it reads `junior`. 2. **Junior = the teammate.** Not a mascot, not a robot face. If a glyph is used, it is abstract: a *node*, a *prompt caret*, a *commit branch*, a *hand-off arrow*. 3. **It must survive 16px.** If it needs more than two shapes, it fails. ### Recommended construction (decision to ratify) - **Glyph:** the `x` of *codx* treated as a **connection node** — two crossing strokes with one dot at the intersection. Geometric, 2 shapes, works at 16px. - **Wordmark:** lowercase `codx-junior` set in the interface family, `-0.01em` tracking, `600` weight, with the hyphen in brand magenta. - **Lockups:** horizontal (glyph + wordmark), stacked (glyph above wordmark), glyph-only (app icon, favicon, avatar). > Alternative if a purely typographic brand is preferred: keep the wordmark as the > only logo and use the magenta hyphen as the glyph. Cheaper, still distinctive, and > it removes the icon problem entirely. **Decide between these two and stop.** --- ## 3. Anatomy & construction rules | Rule | Value | | --- | --- | | Glyph geometry | Strokes on a 4-unit grid; stroke width = 1/8 of glyph height | | Glyph corner radius | `--radius-field` (6px at 1×) applied optically, rounded joins | | Wordmark optical size | Cap height equals 0.72 × glyph height in the horizontal lockup | | Gap glyph → wordmark | 0.5 × glyph width | | Clear space (all sides) | ≥ 0.5 × glyph height, and never less than the height of the `c` | | Minimum sizes | Glyph-only: **16px**. Horizontal lockup: **88px wide**. # Colour System

**Status:** tokens defined here; **not yet wired into the codebase**
(see `00-audit/ui-audit.md` §2). Until they are, the app runs on stock daisyUI themes.

Contrast ratios below are computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula
against the stated backgrounds. They are reproducible: keep the function in
`design/tokens/contrast.md` honest if values change.

---

## 1. The error we are correcting

Three palettes currently coexist:

| Source | Primary | Problem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client/src/assets/main.css` (live) | `#CC0099` | Applied only to `.codx-primary` / `.text-codx-secondary` |
| `client/src/assets/daisy-override.css` (dead) | `#CC049C` | Re-tints 35 themes with a *near-miss* of the brand magenta |
| `client/.codx/profiles/Designer/Designer.md` | `#6366F1` (indigo) | A completely different, cool-toned palette |

`#CC0099` vs `#CC049C` is a **3/255 difference in one channel** — invisible to the eye,
but it means "brand colour" is not a single value in the repo. The Designer profile's
indigo was never implemented and must be retired.

**Decision:** `#CC0099` is the brand magenta. `#CC049C` is retired. Indigo is deleted
from the design vocabulary.

---

## 2. Brand ramps (source of truth)

### Magenta (primary signature)

| Token | Hex | OKLCH | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand.magenta.50` | `#FFF0FA` | `oklch(97% 0.02 330)` | Tinted background (light) |
| `brand.magenta.100` | `#FFD6F0` | `oklch(93% 0.05 330)` | Selected row (light) |
| `brand.magenta.200` | `#FFAEE0` | `oklch(86% 0.10 330)` | Borders on tint |
| `brand.magenta.300` | `#FF80CE` | `oklch(77% 0.17 330)` | Dark-mode hover |
| `brand.magenta.400` | `#FF69B4` | `oklch(72% 0.19 340)` | **Primary text/icon on dark** |
| `brand.magenta.500` | `#F530A8` | `oklch(65% 0.25 330)` | Dark-mode primary fill |
| `brand.magenta.600` | **`#CC0099`** | `oklch(56% 0.28 330)` | **Brand. Primary fill on light** |
| `brand.magenta.700` | `#A3007A` | `oklch(48% 0.24 330)` | Pressed |
| `brand.magenta.800` | `#7A005B` | `oklch(38% 0.19 330)` | Deep accent, charts |
| `brand.magenta.900` | `#4D0039` | `oklch(26% 0.12 330)` | Tinted dark background |

The **dark-theme primary is `oklch(65% 0.32 320)`** (`brand.magenta.500`-ish): the same
hue, lightness raised so it can carry text on the dark canvas. This is the single most
important colour decision in the system — see §5.

### Purple (secondary, depth)

| Token | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand.purple.500` | `#B000B0` | Secondary fill (light) |
| `brand.purple.600` | **`#8F008F`** | Brand secondary. Depth, gradients, chart series 2 |
| `brand.purple.700` | `#6B006B` | Gradient end, pressed |
| `brand.purple.400` | `#C24AC2` | Secondary text on dark |

> `#8F008F` on the dark canvas is **1.8:1** — it is a *fill and gradient* colour only.
> Never use it for text on dark.

---

## 3. Neutrals (surfaces & text)

The neutral ramp is **blue-slate** (hue ≈ 240–250), not pure grey: it keeps magenta
from vibrating and matches the product's "workbench" feel.

### Dark (default theme)

| Token | Value | Hex (reference) | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `surface.base` | `oklch(18% 0.04 240)` | ≈ `#1F2937` | App canvas |
| `surface.raised` | `oklch(22% 0.04 240)` | ≈ `#273244` | Panels, cards, sidebar |
| `surface.overlay` | `oklch(26% 0.04 240)` | ≈ `#2F3A4D` | Modals, popovers, hover |
| `surface.sunken` | `oklch(15% 0.03 240)` | ≈ `#161E29` | Code blocks, wells, inputs |
| `border.subtle` | `base-content / 5%` | — | Dividers |
| `border.default` | `base-content / 10%` | — | Cards, inputs |
| `border.strong` | `base-content / 20%` | — | Active/focus borders |
| `text.primary` | `oklch(96% 0.02 240)` | ≈ `#F3F4F6` | Body |
| `text.secondary` | `base-content / 70%` | — | Labels, metadata |
| `text.tertiary` | `base-content / 55%` | — | Hints, timestamps |
| `text.disabled` | `base-content / 40%` | — | Disabled |

### Light

| Token | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surface.base` | `#FFFFFF` | Canvas |
| `surface.raised` | `#FAFAFC` | Panels |
| `surface.overlay` | `#F0F0F5` | Modals, hover |
| `surface.sunken` | `#F3F4F6` | Code, wells |
| `text.primary` | `#14141E` | Body |
| `text.secondary` | `#3F3F52` | Labels |
| `text.tertiary` | `#6B7280` | Hints |

**Rule of opacity:** hierarchy is built with *opacity of `base-content`*, never with a
new grey. This is what keeps 400+ components visually consistent across both themes.

---

## 4. Semantic colours

Identical hues in both themes; only lightness changes.

| Token | Dark | Light | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | `oklch(75% 0.22 220)` | `#4696DC` | Neutral information, links |
| `success` | `oklch(68% 0.28 140)` | `#3CB450` | Saved, passed, merged, connected |
| `warning` | `oklch(82% 0.26 70)` | `#FFB428` | Budget, retry, degraded, needs review |
| `error` | `oklch(68% 0.32 25)` | `#F05050` | Failed, destructive, blocked |

**Never** use `danger`/`error` red for decoration, and **never** use brand magenta to
signal an error state — magenta means *codx-junior*, not *bad*.

---

## 5. Contrast verification (the part that constrains the design)

Measured against the dark canvas `#1F2937` and white:

| Foreground | On `#1F2937` (dark) | On `#FFFFFF` (light) | AA body (4.5) | AA large / UI (3.0) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#CC0099` brand magenta | **3.1 : 1** ❌ | **4.8 : 1** ✅ | fails on dark | passes on dark (barely) |
| `#FF69B4` pink | **5.5 : 1** ✅ | 2.0 : 1 ❌ | passes on dark | — |
| `#8F008F` purple | **1.8 : 1** ❌ | 8.2 : 1 ✅ | fails on dark | fails on dark |
| `#FFFFFF` on `#CC0099` fill | **4.8 : 1** ✅ | — | ✅ buttons | ✅ |
| `#FFFFFF` on `#FF69B4` fill | 2.0 : 1 ❌ | — | ❌ | ❌ |
| `#111827` on `#FF69B4` fill | 10.4 : 1 ✅ | — | ✅ | ✅ |

### The four resulting rules

1. **On dark, magenta text is pink.** Brand magenta `#CC0099` is used as a *fill*
   (with white text, 4.8:1) or as a *border/graphic*; the moment it becomes text,
   switch to `#FF69B4` (5.5:1) or the OKLCH-boosted primary.
2. **On dark, purple is never text.** Gradient stops and chart series only.
3. **On light, pink is never text.** Light theme uses `#CC0099` for text and
   `#CC0099`/`#8F008F` for fills.
4. **Pink fills need dark text.** White on pink fails; ink on pink passes.

This is why the (unused) `codx-junior-dark.css` boosted primary to
`oklch(65% 0.32 320)`. That instinct was right; the file just never loaded.

---

## 6. Application map (what gets which colour)

| Surface / element | Dark | Light |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App canvas | `surface.base` | `surface.base` |
| Sidebar | `surface.base` + right border `border.subtle` | `surface.raised` |
| Panel / tab bar | `surface.raised` | `surface.raised` |
| Card | `surface.raised` + `border.subtle` | `#FFF` + `border.default` |
| Modal | `surface.overlay` + `border.default` | `#FFF` + `border.default` |
| Primary button | `brand.magenta.600` fill, white text | same |
| Secondary button | `base-content/5` fill, `base-content/80` text | `base-content/5` |
| Ghost button | transparent → `base-content/5` hover | same |
| Destructive button | `error` fill, white text | `error` fill |
| Focus ring | `primary/50`, 2px | `primary/50`, 2px |
| Active nav item | `primary/15` bg + `primary` text + 2px left border | `primary/10` |
| Selected tab (dockview) | `text.primary` + `primary` underline | same |
| AI-authored content | 2px `primary/30` left border | same |
| Human-authored content | 2px `neutral/30` left border | same |
| Code block | `surface.sunken` | `surface.sunken` |
| Diff add / remove | `success/15` / `error/15` bg | `success/10` / `error/10` |
| Charts (series order) | `primary` → `secondary` → `info` → `success` → `warning` → `error` | same |

---

## 7. Data-visualisation palette

Ordered series, chosen for hue separation in both themes:

```
1  #CC0099   magenta   (brand)
2  #8F008F   purple
3  #4696DC   info blue
4  #3CB450   success green
5  #FFB428   warning amber
6  #F05050   error red
7  #7C5CFF   violet      (only in charts)
8  #14B8A6   teal        (only in charts)
```

Rules: sequential = single hue, 4 steps of lightness; categorical = the order above;
never more than 6 series on one chart; always pair colour with a label or pattern.

---

## 8. The 10% rule

Measured on any primary screen, brand magenta should cover **≤ 10% of pixels** —
a primary button, an active nav item, a status dot, a chart line. If a screen is more
than ~10% magenta, the design has lost hierarchy: reduce the accent surface, do not
add another colour.

---

## 9. Implementation notes

- Emit tokens once, as CSS variables on `:root` / `[data-theme]`, generated from
  `design/tokens/design-tokens.json`.
- Prefer **OKLCH** definitions: the dark/light relationship then becomes a lightness
  swap instead of a separate palette.
- Opacity is expressed with `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-base-content) 70%, transparent)`
  — the pattern already used in `base.css`, and it degrades correctly.
- **Do not** add a third theme. Two themes, one brand.

# Typography

**Status:** stack and scale defined; **webfont decision pending** (§2).

The product has **two voices**: the interface speaks in a neutral system UI font, the
machine speaks in monospace. Everything else is scale and rhythm.

---

## 1. The two voices (the core rule)

| Voice | Face | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Interface** | system UI sans | Chrome, buttons, labels, headings, prose, chat messages |
| **Machine** | monospace | Commands, paths, hashes, diffs, logs, token counts, IDs, JSON, YAML, code |

> Test: if a user could copy the string into a terminal and it would mean something,
> it is monospace. This single rule is what makes the product read as *technical and
> calm* instead of *generic SaaS*.

---

## 2. Families

### Interface (in use today)

```css
--font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue",
             Arial, "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
```

Why keep the system stack rather than ship a webfont:

- zero load cost on a product whose critical path is already heavy (Monaco, dockview);
- native feel and correct hinting on every OS;
- no licensing question for a company that has none yet.

**If (and only if) a signature typeface is wanted for marketing/decks**, choose one
variable sans with a wide weight range and a technical personality, and use it
**only** for headings ≥ 24px and marketing surfaces. Never for UI body text — mixing a
webfont into dense tables is where consistency dies.

### Machine (fix required)

Today:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: Droid Sans Mono;
  src: url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Droid Sans Mono"); /* ❌ a stylesheet, not a font */
}
```

A CSS URL cannot be a font `src`, so the face never loads and the browser falls back
to generic `monospace`. Two acceptable outcomes:

| Option | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. System mono** (recommended) | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace` | Zero cost, no licence, correct everywhere |
| **B. Shipped mono** | Self-host one variable mono (`woff2`, subset Latin) in `client/public/fonts/` | Needed only if brand consistency in code samples across OSes is a requirement |

Either way, **remove the broken `@font-face`** and stop referencing a remote font.

---

## 3. Scale

Eight steps. Body is `14px` in dense product surfaces and `16px` in reading surfaces
(chat prose, docs). Never below `12px` except for the mobile tab-bar label (`10px`,
an accepted exception because the label is redundant with a 20px icon).

| Token | Size | Line height | Weight | Tracking | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text.display` | 36px / 2.25rem | 40px | 600 | -0.02em | Landing hero, empty states |
| `text.h1` | 24px / 1.5rem | 32px | 600 | -0.01em | View titles, page headers |
| `text.h2` | 20px / 1.25rem | 28px | 600 | -0.01em | Section headers, modal titles |
| `text.h3` | 16px / 1rem | 24px | 600 | 0 | Card titles, group headers |
| `text.body` | 14px / 0.875rem | 20px | 400 | 0 | Default UI text |
| `text.body-lg` | 16px / 1rem | 26px | 400 | 0 | Chat prose, docs, settings descriptions |
| `text.label` | 12px / 0.75rem | 16px | 500 | 0.01em | Form labels, metadata, badges |
| `text.mono` | 13px / 0.8125rem | 20px | 400 | 0 | Inline code, IDs, counts |
| `text.code` | 14px / 0.875rem | 20px | 400 | 0 | Code blocks (today 16px/19px — see §5) |

### Weight usage

`400` body · `500` labels and interactive text · `600` headings only.
**Never `700+`** (with system UI it turns shouty), **never `300`** on dark
(hairlines disappear on low-DPI).

### Numbers

Any column of numbers (tables, costs, durations, token counts) uses
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and, where it is a machine value, monospace.
This is already the pattern in `DesktopSidebar.vue` (`font-mono font-semibold tabular-nums`)
and should become a rule, not a lucky habit.

---

## 4. Line length & density

| Context | Measure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat message | 62–78 characters (`max-width: 800px`) | Centred column on wide screens |
| Documentation / wiki | 70 characters | `max-width: 68ch` |
| Tables & logs | no limit — horizontal scroll allowed | Density wins; never wrap a hash |
| Forms | `max-width: 480px` per field group | Labels above, hints below |
| Modal body | `max-width: 672px` (`md:max-w-2xl`, as today) | — |

**Paragraph spacing** `12px` (`text.body`) between blocks, `0` between list items.

---

## 5. Code typography (current vs target)

Today in `client/src/assets/main.css`:

```css
.view-code pre, .view-code code.hljs {
  font-family: "Droid Sans Mono", "monospace", monospace !important;
  font-size: 16px !important;
  line-height: 19px !important;
  letter-spacing: 0px !important;
  font-feature-settings: "liga" 0, "calt" 0 !important;   /* ✅ keep: no ligature confusion */
  max-height: 600px !important;
}
```

Target:

```css
font-family: var(--font-mono);
font-size: 14px;          /* 16px is too large for side-by-side diffs */
line-height: 20px;        /* ratio 1.43 — must stay fixed, never em-based */
letter-spacing: 0;
font-feature-settings: "liga" 0, "calt" 0;  /* keep */
tab-size: 2;                                 /* add: 4 spaces breaks diff alignment */
```

Monospace line height must be an **absolute px value**, not relative: diff rows are
aligned by pixel, and any rounding drifts the gutter.

---

## 6. Headings semantics

- One `h1` per view (the view title in the header bar).
- Modal titles are `h2`; card titles inside a view are `h3`.
- The visual size never decides the heading level — use the tag the document outline
  needs and style separately (avoids the `h3`-styled-as-`h1` accessibility smell that
  exists in several dialogs today).

---

## 7. Truncation & overflow

| Content | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Chat title / project name in a rail | Single line, `truncate`, tooltip with full value |
| File path | Truncate in the middle (`foo/…/bar.ts`), never at the end |
| Commit subject | Single line truncate; full text in the detail panel |
| Command / log line | No truncation. Wrap with hanging indent, or scroll horizontally |
| Table cell with a hash | No wrap; `overflow-x: auto` on the container |

---

## 8. Copy-in-code guidelines

```
✅ "Saved"                        ❌ "Successfully saved!"
✅ "12 files changed"             ❌ "12 file(s) changed"
✅ "3m 12s"                       ❌ "3 minutes and 12 seconds"
✅ "claude-sonnet-4-5"            ❌ "Claude Sonnet 4.5" (in a machine field)
✅ "codx-junior"                  ❌ "CodxJunior"
```

Capitalisation: sentence case for everything (`Save changes`, not `Save Changes`).
Exception: product/feature proper nouns (`Task Manager`, `Global Settings` — as already
used in `config/apps.js` titles).

---

## 9. Checklist for a new surface

- [ ] Only the two voices (UI sans / mono); no third family.
- [ ] Type sizes come from the scale above; no one-off `text-[17px]`.
- [ ] Body ≥ 14px; nothing below 12px; mobile tab label is the only 10px exception.
- [ ] Numbers in columns are tabular (and mono if machine-generated).
- [ ] Line length within the measure for the context.
- [ ] Heading tags match the outline, not the visual size.
- [ ] Truncation rule applied per content type.

request.content:
# Voice & Tone

How codx-junior speaks. Applies to every string in the product, the docs, the error
messages and the marketing site.

---

## 1. Voice (constant)

**An experienced teammate who happens to be a machine.**

- **Direct.** State the fact, then the action. "Build failed. 2 tests, `auth.spec.ts`."
- **Specific.** Names, numbers, paths, durations. Never "something went wrong".
- **Calm.** No exclamation marks. No "Oops!". No emojis in errors.
- **Honest about uncertainty.** "I couldn't reach the container" beats "An unexpected
  error occurred".
- **Second person, active.** "You can retry" / "codx-junior is running the tests".

**Not:** a mascot, a hype-man, a helpdesk script, a lawyer.

---

## 2. Tone by context

| Context | Tone | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty state | Inviting, one action | **No chats yet.** Start one and codx-junior will pick up your project context. `[New chat]` |
| Working / streaming | Terse status, present continuous | `Running tests… 3 of 12` · `Reading api/chat/chat_engine.py` |
| Success | One word, or one line + detail | `Merged` · `PR #128 merged into main. 4 files changed.` |
| Warning (budget, limits) | Factual + the threshold | `Daily budget at 82%. Runs will pause at 100%.` |
| Error (recoverable) | What happened + what to do | **Couldn't reach the API.** Check the container is running, then retry. `[Retry]` `[View logs]` |
| Error (user-caused) | Neutral, no blame, no humour | `Name is required.` not `You forgot the name!` |
| Destructive confirm | Consequence first, verb last | **Delete board "Sprint 12"?** 14 tasks will be removed. This can't be undone. `[Cancel]` `[Delete board]` |
| Handover to human | Explicit, no ambiguity | `Waiting for you — login required.` `[Take over]` |
| AI-generated prose | Neutral, no self-reference | "The endpoint returns 404 when the project is archived." (not "I think that…") |

---

## 3. Micro-rules

| Rule | Do | Don't |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sentence case everywhere | `Save changes` | `Save Changes` |
| Verbs on buttons, noun elsewhere | `Delete board` / `Board deleted` | `Deletion` |
| Second person for humans, third for the agent | `You paused the run` / `codx-junior paused the run` | `We paused` |
| Numbers as digits | `3 files`, `2m 12s` | `three files` |
| Units always | `12.4k tokens`, `$0.42`, `1.2 GB` | `12.4k`, `0.42` |
| Ellipsis for in-progress, not for menus | `Deleting…` | `Settings…` |
| No trailing period on labels/buttons | `Run tests` | `Run tests.` |
| Period at the end of sentences in body/errors | `Retry to continue.` | `Retry to continue` |
| Max ~90 characters per toast | `Saved` / `Copied to clipboard` | A paragraph |

---

## 4. Vocabulary (use these words, not those)

| Use | Instead of | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **chat** | conversation, thread, session | The product term |
| **task** | ticket, issue, card (except visually) | A task is the unit of work |
| **board** / **column** / **card** | kanban, lane | Familiar to the user |
| **run** | job, execution, orchestration | `harness run` |
| **step** | subtask, phase, stage | One unit of a run |
| **profile** | persona, agent role, bot | A profile has instructions and tools |
| **team** | group, org | Teams contain humans *and* profiles |
| **workspace** | environment, sandbox, container app | A workspace *runs in* a container |
| **project** | repo, workspace | A project may have several repos |
| **knowledge** | RAG, embeddings, vectors | Never expose the implementation |
| **take over** | intervene, hijack, assume control | The human/AI handover |
| **budget** / **cxjcoins** | credits, quota, tokens | `cxjcoins` is the currency name |
| **AI** (as adjective) | artificial intelligence, LLM (in UI) | `AI models`, not `LLM models` in chrome |

Identifiers stay machine-formatted in machine contexts: `software_developer`,
`claude-sonnet-4-5`, `codx-junior-harness`.

---

## 5. Error message formula

```
[What failed]. [Why, if known]. [What to do next].
```

Examples (all real product situations):

```
✅ Couldn't start the container. Port 8080 is already in use. Stop the other service or change the port.
✅ Git push rejected. The remote has 3 commits you don't have. Pull first, then push again.
✅ Indexing paused. Milvus isn't reachable. Check the milvus container, then resume.
✅ Request timed out after 120s. The model may be overloaded. Retry, or switch to a smaller model.
```

Anti-patterns:

```
❌ Something went wrong.
❌ Error: [object Object]
❌ Oops! Looks like the request failed 😢
❌ Unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.   (which action? which error?)
```

---

## 6. Accessibility of copy

- **Name the control in the label.** Icon-only buttons get `aria-label` with the same
  words as a visible tooltip: `aria-label="Close modal"`, not `"X"`.
- **Never colour-only meaning.** Pair every status colour with a word or icon
  (`● online` / `● offline`, already the pattern in `DesktopSidebar.vue`).
- **Link text is meaningful out of context.** `View the failed step`, not `click here`.
- **Abbreviations expanded on first use in a surface**, or in the tooltip
  (`PR` → `Pull request`, `cxj` → `cxjcoins`).
- **Locale**: strings are English today; write them so they can be translated —
  no concatenated sentences, no text inside images, no plural-by-suffix hacks
  (`1 file` / `2 files` must be two keys).

---

## 7. Placeholders & empty states

Every list/board/table needs all three states designed:

| State | Content |
| --- | --- |
| **Empty (first use)** | One sentence of what this is + one primary action. No illustration required. |
| **Empty (filtered)** | "No results for `auth`." + `Clear filters`. Never the first-use text. |
| **Loading** | Skeleton with the real layout, or a single centred spinner if < 300ms. Never a spinner that replaces a full page for a table refresh. |

Current gap: the boot screen reads *"Wake up, codx-junior..."* (`App.vue`). It is
charming once; it is confusing on a cold production start. Replace with
`Starting codx-junior…` and keep personality for the landing page.

---

## 8. Review checklist (paste into PRs touching UI copy)

- [ ] Sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emojis in errors.
- [ ] Error follows *what / why / next*.
- [ ] Buttons are verbs; confirmations repeat the verb (`Delete board`).
- [ ] Numbers have units; times are `2m 12s`; money has its symbol.
- [ ] Vocabulary matches §4 (quick scan: "conversation", "bot", "quota" are red flags).
- [ ] Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` matching its tooltip.
- [ ] Strings are translation-safe (no concatenation, no embedded HTML).

request.content:
# Design Foundations

Space, radius, elevation, motion, icons, layering and layout grids.
These are the primitives every component composes; they are the part that must not
drift.

**Implementation target:** Tailwind v4 `@theme` variables generated from
`design/tokens/design-tokens.json`. Until then, values below are the reference and the
current implementation is noted for comparison.

---

## 1. Spacing — 4px base, 8px rhythm

Tailwind's scale is already 4px-based (`1 = 0.25rem`). Use it; do not invent pixels.

| Token | px | rem | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `space.0-5` | 2 | 0.125 | Optical nudges only |
| `space.1` | 4 | 0.25 | Icon ↔ label |
| `space.1-5` | 6 | 0.375 | Inside badges/chips |
| `space.2` | 8 | 0.5 | Inside buttons, tight stacks |
| `space.3` | 12 | 0.75 | List row padding, control gaps |
| `space.4` | 16 | 1 | Card padding, form field gap |
| `space.5` | 20 | 1.25 | Section inner padding |
| `space.6` | 24 | 1.5 | Panel padding, region gap |
| `space.8` | 32 | 2 | Between major sections |
| `space.12` | 48 | 3 | Page-level breathing |

**Rhythm rule:** vertical spacing between siblings comes from `2 / 3 / 4`;
spacing *between regions* from `6 / 8`. Mixing the two is what makes dense UIs feel
simultaneously cramped and scattered.

Density: this product is **compact by default** (`13–14px` text, `12px` row padding).
A "comfortable" density is not offered — it would break the tables users rely on.

---

## 2. Radius

| Token | Value | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `radius.field` | `0.375rem` (6px) | Inputs, selects, small buttons, checkboxes |
| `radius.box` | `0.5rem` (8px) | Cards, panels, dropdowns, toasts |
| `radius.selector` | `0.75rem` (12px) | Tabs, segmented controls, nav items, mobile icon buttons |
| `radius.modal` | `0.75rem` (12px) | Dialogs |
| `radius.full` | `9999px` | Pills, avatars, status dots, tags |

The daisyUI theme already declares `--radius-selector: 0.75rem`, `--radius-field:
0.375rem`, `--radius-box: 0.5rem` — **keep these three names**, they are the contract.
One inconsistency to fix: `Modal.vue` uses `rounded-lg` (8px) while the mobile icon
buttons use `rounded-xl` (12px); dialogs should be `radius.modal` (12px).

**Never mix radii inside one component.** A card with a 12px body, an 8px header and a
9999px button reads as three objects.

---

## 3. Elevation

Dark UIs cannot rely on shadows; elevation is communicated by **surface lightness +
border + blur**.

| Level | Dark | Light | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 flat | `surface.base` | `#FFF` | Canvas, panels |
| 1 raised | `surface.raised` + `border.subtle` | `#FFF` + `border.default` | Cards, sidebar sections |
| 2 overlay | `surface.overlay` + `border.default` + `shadow-lg` | `#FFF` + `shadow-lg` | Dropdowns, popovers, toasts |
| 3 modal | `surface.overlay` + `border.default` + `shadow-2xl` + backdrop `blur-sm` | same | Dialogs |

Rules: no shadow on flat surfaces; no `shadow-xl` on inline elements; the backdrop of a
modal is `bg-base-100/60 backdrop-blur-sm` (already the pattern in `Modal.vue` — keep it).

---

## 4. Motion

| Token | Duration | Easing | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion.instant` | 0ms | — | State that must feel native (press, toggle) |
| `motion.fast` | 150ms | `ease` | Hover, focus, colour, opacity |
| `motion.base` | 200ms | `ease` | Sidebar width, tab change, menu open |
| `motion.slow` | 300ms | `ease` | Modal enter, panel expand |
| `motion.sheet` | 240ms | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | Mobile sheets (already in `base.css`) |

Rules:

1. **Only animate `transform` and `opacity`.** Never animate `width`/`height` on a
   surface that scrolls or contains a virtualised list (the sidebar's `w-16 ⇄ w-64`
   transition is 200ms of layout thrash on every toggle — acceptable today, but do not
   copy it into new surfaces; use `transform: translateX` + a fixed-width container).
2. **Never loop** except an explicit in-progress indicator (spinner, pulse dot).
3. **Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.** `base.css` already disables the mobile shell
   transitions; extend that to every new transition group.
4. **No entrance animation on content that streams.** Messages appear; they do not slide.

---

## 5. Iconography

- **Set:** Font Awesome 6.5.1 Free, vendored at
  `client/src/assets/fontawesome-free-6.5.1-web`, used as `<i class="fa-solid fa-*">`.
  A second library (`@iconify/vue`) is installed — pick **one** per surface; the
  recommendation is FA for chrome (already everywhere) and Iconify only for brand
  logos/marks that FA does not have.
- **Styles:** `fa-solid` for UI and status; `fa-regular` for "soft" navigation and
  empty states; `fa-brands` for third-party products (GitHub, VS Code…).
- **Sizes:** `12px` inline with `12px` label · `14px` in rows and buttons · `16px` in
  section headers · `20px` in the mobile tab bar · `24px` in empty states.
- **Colour:** inherits `currentColor`. Never hard-code an icon colour.
- **Decorative icons must be `aria-hidden="true"`** (already the pattern in
  `MobileTabBar.vue`); icon-only buttons need `aria-label`.
- **Stroke vs fill:** FA solid is already a filled style; do not mix in a line-icon set
  in the same view.
- **Do not use emoji as icons** in UI chrome. They render differently per OS and cannot
  be recoloured.

**Icon choice consistency (fix list):** `fa-comments` (regular) is used for both *Chat*
and *Messenger* in `config/apps.js` and `config/mobile.js`. They are different apps —
give them distinct glyphs (`fa-comments` / `fa-inbox` or `fa-paper-plane`).

---

## 6. Layering (z-index)

The audit found an unordered ladder; a modal at `z-50` can paint **below** the mobile
sidebar at `z-150` (`00-audit/ui-audit.md` §8.3). This is the replacement scale —
a single source of truth, spaced by 10 so future layers fit between.

| Token | z | Occupant (today → target) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `z.base` | 0 | Page content |
| `z.raised` | 10 | Sticky headers, in-flow toolbars |
| `z.sticky` | 20 | Table headers, board column headers |
| `z.tabbar` | 30 | Mobile tab bar (`MobileTabBar` — already `z-30`) |
| `z.chrome` | 50 | Desktop sidebar (currently `z-50`, keep) |
| `z.backdrop` | 100 | Mobile nav backdrop (currently `z-100`, keep) |
| `z.toast` | 130 | Toasts (currently `z-[130]`, keep) |
| `z.nav` | 150 | Mobile launcher / sheet panel (currently `z-150`, keep) |
| `z.modal` | 160 | **Dialogs — move from `50` to `160`** |
| `z.popper` | 200 | Reka/dropdown portals (currently `200`, keep — must stay above everything) |

Rule: a portalled surface is always above the surface that opened it, and **toasts are
above modals** (a failure inside a dialog must be visible). Verify after the change:
open a dialog on mobile with the launcher closed, then open a dropdown inside it.

---

## 7. Layout grid

### Desktop (≥ 1280px)

```
┌──────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ rail │  dockview workspace                           │
│ 64px │  ┌────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┐  │
│  or  │  │ chat   │ changes      │ preview         │  │
│ 256px│  │ 30%    │ 33%          │ 37%             │  │
└──────┴──┴────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────┘  │
```

- Sidebar: `64px` collapsed / `256px` expanded (`w-16` / `w-64`).
- Panels: resizable, widths persisted in `ui.panelWidths` (`chat 30`, `changes 33`,
  `preview 37`); minimum panel width **280px**.
- Content max width for prose: `68ch`; tables/logs: full width.
- Sash/drag target: visual seam 4px (dockview-fixed), **pointer target 10px** — already
  implemented via pseudo-elements in `main.css`; copy that technique for any new splitter.

### Tablet & mobile (≤ 1024px — JS breakpoint)

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│ MobileTopBar  (56px)│  ← title + back + actions
├─────────────────────┤
│ content (scroll)    │  ← 16px side padding
├─────────────────────┤
│ MobileTabBar  (60px)│  ← + safe-area-inset-bottom
└─────────────────────┘
```

- One column. No side-by-side panes; use a **sheet** or a **route** instead.
- Horizontal board scrolling: `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`, one column at a time
  (already in `base.css`).
- Touch targets ≥ 44×44px; 8px minimum gap.
- Modal → `fullscreen` variant (`100dvh`, no radius) — already supported.

**Breakpoint table** (single source):

| Name | Range | Shell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mobile` | 0–640px | Mobile shell |
| `tablet` | 641–1024px | **Mobile shell** (by design; verify with users) |
| `desktop` | 1025–1535px | Desktop sidebar `64px` + dockview |
| `wide` | ≥ 1536px | Desktop, three panes visible |

The `≤1024px` boundary is decided in JS (`store/ui.js → handleResize`), so CSS
`md:`/`lg:` utilities alone cannot compensate: **any layout you write must be checked
against `isMobile`, not only against the viewport width.**

---

## 8. Focus, hover, active, disabled, loading (state contract)

Every interactive component must define all six. Shared recipe:

| State | Visual |
| --- | --- |
| Default | `bg-base-content/5` (secondary) or `bg-primary` (primary) |
| Hover | `+5%` surface lightness, **150ms**; never a colour change for the primary fill |
| Focus-visible | `outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary)`, `outline-offset: 2px` — or the existing `ring-2 ring-primary/50`; must be visible on both themes |
| Active/pressed | `transform: scale(0.98)` (or `active:scale-95` as used today) + one step darker, **0ms** transition |
| Disabled | `opacity: 0.5`, `cursor: not-allowed`, no hover, `aria-disabled="true"` |
| Loading | Spinner replaces the icon, label unchanged, `aria-busy="true"`, pointer-events off |

Rules: never remove the focus ring; never use colour alone to signal state; a disabled
control must not be the only way to discover why an action is unavailable (show a
reason in a tooltip).

---

## 9. Token implementation target

```css
/* client/src/assets/tokens.css — generated from design/tokens/design-tokens.json */
@theme {
  --color-brand-50:  oklch(97% 0.02 330);
  --color-brand-600: oklch(56% 0.28 330);   /* #CC0099 */
  --color-brand-400: oklch(72% 0.19 340);   /* #FF69B4 */
  --radius-field: 0.375rem;
  --radius-box: 0.5rem;
  --radius-selector: 0.75rem;
  --font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
}
```

Then:
1. Register exactly two daisyUI themes (`codx-junior-dark`, `codx-junior-light`)
   instead of `themes: all`.
2. Delete `daisy-override.css` and `assets/themes/*.css` (dead code — see audit §2).
3. Delete `client/src/assets/logo.svg` (the Vue logo).
4. Fix the broken `@font-face` in `main.css`.
5. Add a lint rule / grep in CI: no raw hex outside `tokens.css`
   (`rg -n "#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}" client/src --glob '!**/tokens.css'`).

---

## 10. Foundations checklist

- [ ] Spacing from the Tailwind scale only; no arbitrary `p-[17px]`.
- [ ] Radius from the three named tokens; one radius per component.
- [ ] Elevation via surface + border, shadow only for overlay/modal.
- [ ] Every transition ≤ 300ms, `transform`/`opacity` only, reduced-motion respected.
- [ ] Icons: one set per surface, `aria-hidden` on decorative, `aria-label` on icon-only.
- [ ] New portal surface uses the `z` ladder, not a new number.
- [ ] Layout checked at 390 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1920 px **and** with `isMobile` true/false.
- [ ] All six interaction states defined.

request.content:
# Component Specifications

Core components with their **states**, **tokens** and the **current implementation**
in `client/`. Each entry says *keep* (already correct), *align* (exists, needs tokens) or
*build* (missing) so the work is schedulable.

Anatomy is described with the token names from `design/tokens/design-tokens.json`.

---

## 1. Button

**Status:** align (daisyUI `btn` is used throughout, with size drift).

| Variant | Background | Text | Border |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | `brand.magenta.600` | `#FFFFFF` | none |
| Secondary | `base-content / 5%` | `base-content / 80%` | `base-content / 10%` |
| Ghost | transparent | `base-content / 70%` | none |
| Danger | `error` | `#FFFFFF` | none |
| Link | transparent | `primary` | underline on hover |

| Size | Height | Padding-x | Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 28px | 10px | `text.label` (12/500) |
| `md` | 32px | 12px | `text.body` (14/500) |
| `lg` | 40px | 16px | `text.body` (14/600) |

States: default / hover (+5% light) / `focus-visible` (2px ring `primary/50`, offset 2) /
active (`scale .98`) / disabled (`opacity .5`, `cursor-not-allowed`) / loading
(spinner left, label kept, `aria-busy`).

Rules: one primary button per surface region. Icon-only buttons are **32×32 minimum**
(44×44 on mobile) and require `aria-label`. Never use `btn` default padding for a
toolbar — toolbars use `btn btn-ghost btn-sm` uniformly.

---

## 2. Input, textarea, select

**Status:** align. Current patterns use `bg-white/5 border-white/10` in places
(Designer profile) and daisyUI `input` elsewhere — the target is one recipe:

```
height 32px (md) / 40px (lg, mobile)
padding 8px 12px
bg surface.sunken
border 1px border.default  →  focus: primary/50 + ring 2 primary/20
radius radius.field (6px)
text text.body, placeholder text.tertiary
```

- Label above (`text.label`, 12/500, `text.secondary`), hint below (`text.tertiary`).
- Error: border `error`, message below with `fa-circle-exclamation`, `aria-invalid="true"`
  and `aria-describedby` pointing at the message.
- **Mobile inputs are `font-size: 16px` minimum** — enforced today by `base.css` to stop
  iOS zoom; do not override it.
- Search inputs: leading `fa-magnifying-glass`, trailing clear button, `role="searchbox"`.

---

## 3. Card / panel

**Status:** keep (visual) → align (tokens).

```
bg surface.raised
border 1px border.subtle
radius radius.box (8px)
padding 16px
hover: border.default + bg raised+2%
```

Used for: task cards, project cards, profile cards, workspace cards, provider cards.
The *task card* variant adds: `radius.selector` (12px) on board view, a 3px left status
accent, title `text.body` 2-line clamp, meta row (`text.label`, mono for IDs/counts).

---

## 4. Modal / dialog

**Status:** keep — this is the best-specified component in the codebase
(`client/src/components/Modal.vue`). Two changes: raise `z-50 → z-160`, and add a
focus trap.

Spec (matches the current implementation, which should not regress):

```
backdrop  fixed inset-0 bg-base-100/60 backdrop-blur-sm
box       bg-base-300 radius.modal border border.default shadow-2xl
          max-h-[90vh]  width: full on mobile, md:max-w-2xl
header    only when a title or header slot exists; py-2 px-4/6, border-b border.subtle
body      px-6 py-4, overflow-y auto
footer    only when a footer slot exists; border-t, right aligned, gap 12px
fullscreen 100dvh, radius 0, no shadow (mobile)
```

- `Escape` closes; `@close` is the single close channel; click on backdrop closes only
  if `close` is set.
- **Accessibility (must add):** move focus to the dialog on open, trap `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`
  inside, restore focus to the trigger on close, `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`
  `aria-labelledby` = title id.
- Confirm dialogs: title states the consequence, footer is `[Cancel] [Verb]` with the
  destructive verb last (`ConfirmDialog.vue` exists — use it, do not hand-roll).

---

## 5. Toast / notification

**Status:** keep (`Toast.vue`). Align copy length.

```
position  desktop bottom-4 right-4 · mobile bottom: safe-area + 4.75rem, left/right 12px
z         z.toast (130)
box       alert alert-<type> · radius.box · shadow-lg · max-w-sm
content   icon (type colour) + message (text.body) + dismiss (btn-ghost xs)
timing    auto-dismiss 3000ms, paused on hover (implemented)
stacking  newest last, max 3 visible, drop the oldest
```

Rules: one sentence, ≤ 90 characters. Success may be a single word (`Saved`). Never put
a decision inside a toast — that is a dialog. `aria-live="polite"` on the container.

---

## 6. Status badge / dot

```
badge   inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2.5 py-1 radius.full
        bg <semantic>/20  text <semantic>  text.label/500
dot     size 6px, radius.full, bg <semantic>; optional 1.5px ring <semantic>/30
```

Always pair colour with a word (`● online`, `● offline` — already done in the sidebar).
Status vocabulary is fixed: `online/offline`, `running/paused/failed/done`,
`queued/blocked/review`.

---

## 7. Tabs & segmented control

- `TabNavigation.vue` / dockview tabs: active = `text.primary` + 2px `primary`
  underline (or `primary` text in dockview, already implemented in `main.css`);
  inactive = `text.tertiary`, `opacity .7`.
- Height `32px`, padding-x `12px`, gap `4px`, radius `radius.selector` for the
  segmented variant.
- Keyboard: `←/→` moves, `Home/End` jumps, `tabindex` roving, `role="tablist"`.

---

## 8. Navigation item (sidebar)

```
collapsed 64px rail    · icon 20px centred, tooltip on hover, 40px hit area
expanded  256px        · icon 16px + label text.body + optional badge
inactive  text.base-content/70, hover bg base-content/5
active    bg primary/15 · text primary · 2px left border primary
group     label text.label uppercase? → NO: sentence case, text.tertiary, 12/500
```

Constraint: with `w-16` collapsed, **every icon needs a tooltip and an `aria-label`** —
today the collapsed rail relies on `title` attributes; make them real tooltips.

---

## 9. Data table (logs, tasks, users, models)

**Status:** build a shared spec — five independent implementations exist
(`LogsTable`, `TaskTableView`, `SecurityUserList`, `AIModels`, `Cockpit`-style grids).

```
header    sticky, bg surface.raised, text.label/500 text.secondary, border-b
row       height 36px (compact) / 44px (comfortable), border-b border.subtle
hover     bg base-content/5
selected  bg primary/10
cell      padding-x 12px, truncate single line, mono for machine values
numbers   tabular-nums, right aligned
empty     in-table row: "No results" + optional clear-filters action
loading   skeleton rows (5) with the real column widths
overflow  horizontal scroll on the container, never on the page
```

Sorting indicator: `fa-chevron-up/down` 10px, `text.tertiary` → `text.primary` when active.
Row actions: right-aligned, revealed on hover **and** always visible on touch.

---

## 10. Chat message (the product's most important component)

```
row        flex, gap 12px, mb 16px
avatar     32px rounded-full (AI: brand glyph; human: user avatar)
bubble     max-w-[800px], radius.box, px 16px py 12px
  AI       bg surface.raised, border.subtle, 2px left border primary/30
  human    bg primary/10, border primary/20
meta       text.label, text.tertiary: author · time · model · tokens · cost
code       mono 14/20, bg surface.sunken, radius.field, overflow-x auto
actions    copy · retry · branch, revealed on hover, always visible on touch
streaming  no entrance animation; a single 2px primary cursor at the tail
```

Rules: the human/AI distinction must never rely on colour alone — the left border plus
the avatar plus the author label carry it. Long content must not push the composer: the
message column scrolls, the composer is fixed to the viewport bottom.

---

## 11. Human-in-the-loop / handover state

**Status:** build — this is a brand-level differentiator identified in the audit.

```
banner   full-width, bg warning/15, border-y border warning/30, py 12px px 16px
icon     fa-hand (solid), warning
title    "Waiting for you" (text.body/600)
detail   what the human must do (login, MFA, approval), text.body
actions  [Take over] (primary) · [Skip] (ghost)
```

Applies to: browser sessions (login/captcha), payments, destructive confirmations,
guardrail blocks, budget exhaustion. Both the AI-paused and human-controlling states
must be visually distinct — never the same banner with different text.

---

## 12. Board / kanban

```
column     width 300px (min 280), radius.box, bg surface.raised, border.subtle
header     name + count badge + actions; sticky inside the column
card       3px left accent = status colour, title 2-line clamp,
           meta row: assignees (24px avatars, -6px overlap), due date, tags
drag       lifted card: shadow-lg + rotate(1deg)? → NO rotation. scale 1.02 + shadow-lg
drop       target column: bg primary/5 + 2px dashed primary/30
empty      "No tasks" + `+ Add task` inline
```

Mobile: one column at a time with scroll-snap (already implemented); swipe between
columns; the card tap opens a full-screen sheet, not a side drawer.

---

## 13. Empty state

```
container  centred, max-w-md, py 48px
icon       24px, text.tertiary (regular style, not solid)
title      text.h3, text.primary
body       text.body, text.secondary, ≤ 2 lines
action     one primary button (optional)
```

No illustrations in the product (marketing only). First-use ≠ filtered-empty — see
`01-brand/voice-and-tone.md` §7.

---

## 14. Avatar

```
size    16 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 px (square ratio, rounded-full)
fallback initials on brand.magenta.600 (white text) — derive from the name, not random
group   overlap -6px, ring 2px surface.base
status  optional 8px dot, bottom-right, border 2px surface.base
```

Current gap: avatars come from `api.dicebear.com` (external, off-brand, privacy leak).
Ship a local initial-based fallback and use it as the default.

---

## 15. Loading indicators

| Duration | Indicator |
| --- | --- |
| < 300ms | nothing (avoid flashing) |
| 300ms–2s | inline spinner (`w-4 h-4 border-2 border-primary/30 border-t-primary rounded-full animate-spin`) |
| > 2s | skeleton with real layout, or a progress line with a label |
| > 10s (agent work) | step list: what is running, elapsed time, cancel action |

Never a full-page spinner for a refresh of a section — replace only the affected region.

---

## 16. Component backlog (priority order)

| # | Work | Why | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Emit tokens + two daisyUI themes | Everything else inherits correctness | M |
| 2 | Modal: focus trap, `z-160`, radius token | Accessibility + layering bug | S |
| 3 | Shared `DataTable` primitive | 5 divergent implementations | L |
| 4 | Logo assets + sidebar lockup | Corporate image blocker | M |
| 5 | Handover banner component | Brand promise, used by 4 features | S |
| 6 | Button/Input/Badge recipes as Vue components | Removes drift | M |
| 7 | Chat message spec (incl. streaming/meta row) | Core surface | M |
| 8 | Empty-state component + copy pass | Consistency | S |
| 9 | Local avatar fallback (drop dicebear) | Privacy + brand | S |

request.content:
# Information Architecture & Core Flows

Derived from the two registries that actually drive navigation:
`client/src/config/apps.js` (29 app keys) and `client/src/config/mobile.js`
(4 tabs + 5 launcher groups).

---

## 1. The navigation model (as built)

codx-junior does **not** have pages. It has **apps** that can be opened in two ways:

```
                 ┌──────────────────────────┐
   user action →│  openApp(key, payload)    │
                 └───────────┬──────────────┘
                             │ reads config/apps.js
              ┌──────────────┴───────────────┐
   !isMobile / desktop            isMobile / single
              │                              │
   dockview PANEL (expert)        ROUTE (router)
   multi-instance by params       params in the URL
```

Consequences that must be respected by every design:

- **The same app must look right in both destinations.** A screen designed only as a
  dockview panel will be wrong as a full-page route (no sidebar, its own scroll,
  back button, 60px tab bar).
- **Multi-instance apps open several panels** (`tasks` per board, `browser-viewer` per
  session, `file-viewer` per file, `workspace` per workspace, `team-channel` per
  channel). Their titles must be distinguishable — include the instance name.
- **Deep links are real.** Boards, chats, teams and workspaces encode their identity in
  the URL; a design that hides "where am I" breaks refresh and sharing.

---

## 2. The app catalogue (grouped the way users think)

### Work
| App | Key | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | `home` | Command centre; mobile uses the management dashboard as home |
| Chats | (route `chats`) | Inbox of conversations |
| New chat | — | Primary action, available from every shell |
| Task Manager | `tasks` | Multi-instance (one panel per board) |
| Planning | `planning` | Same component as Task Manager, `view: planning` |
| Company | `company` | Org, hybrid teams, missions, autopilot |
| Management | `management-dashboard` | Cross-project pulse, blockers, delivery, cost |
| Projects | `projects` | Browse every project |
| Harness | `harness` | Runs, worker health, audit journal |

### People
Messenger (`messenger`) · Meet (`meet`) · Team (`team`, plus `team-channel`)

### Build
Files (`file-explorer` / `file-viewer`) · Git (`git-view`) · Workspaces
(`workspaces` / `workspace`) · Browsers (`browser-sessions` / `browser-viewer`) ·
Infrastructure (`infra`) · Wiki (`wiki`) · Docs (`docs`) · Knowledge (`knowledge`)

### Insights
Analytics (`analytics`) · Metrics (`metrics`) · API monitoring (`api-monitoring`) ·
Chat logs (`chat-logs`) · Decision logs (`decision-model-logs`) · Logs (`log-viewer`)

### Account
Project settings (`settings`) · Global settings (`global-settings`) ·
Knowledge settings (`knowledge_settings`, `wiki_settings`) · Account (`account`) ·
Vibe coding (`vibe-coding`) · Solopreneur (`solopreneur`)

---

## 3. Shells

| Shell | Who | Chrome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Desktop** | `!isMobile` | 64/256px sidebar (apps + workspaces + user footer) · dockview workspace · status/toast |
| **Mobile** | `≤1024px` | 56px top bar (title, back, actions) · content · 60px tab bar (Home, Chats, Tasks, More) |
| **Company** | company role | Own tab bar (Company, Ask, Add person, New team, More) — desktop keeps the standard shell |
| **Solopreneur** | full-screen route | Own sidebar/topbar; no codx-junior chrome |

**Design debt to resolve:** desktop hides most apps behind `WindowsMenu` while mobile
hides them behind *More*. Two mental models for one catalogue. Target: **one
"Everything" launcher**, used by both shells, with the same grouping and search
(the mobile `MOBILE_APP_GROUPS` already models it well — promote it to the desktop).

---

## 4. Core flows (the five that matter)

### F1 · Ask for work, watch it happen
```
New chat → pick profile + model → type request
  → assistant streams: thinking → tool call → file change → result
  → artifacts appear inline (diff, PR, card, preview)
  → accept / iterate / hand off
```
Design requirements: the step trace is *always* visible while running; cost and elapsed
time accrue in place; the composer never scrolls away; a completed run collapses to a
summary with an expand affordance.

### F2 · Track the work
```
Board → column → card → chat thread inside the card → done
```
Design requirements: card = task + conversation + artifacts; dragging must not lose
scroll or selection; the board is a *view* of the same tasks as Planning/Sprint/Table.

### F3 · Review a change
```
Git view → branch → PR → file list → diff → comment → merge
```
Design requirements: diff typography is non-negotiable (mono, fixed line-height,
tab-size 2); the file tree, diff and conversation are three panes on desktop, three
routes on mobile; risk/impact summary at the top.

### F4 · Hand a task to a machine session
```
Workspace / Browser / Computer → launch → AI drives → *needs human* → Take over → Give back
```
Design requirements: the live view is the hero; the control lease (who is driving) is
always visible; the handover banner (see `components.md` §11) is the only way to switch.

### F5 · Understand the cost and the health
```
Analytics / Metrics / Harness → window selector → chart → drill into a run
```
Design requirements: one time-window control reused across all insight screens
(`TimeSelector.vue` exists); every number has a unit and a comparison; empty and
partial-data states are designed, not left blank.

---

## 5. Navigation states (must be designed for every screen)

| State | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loading | panel skeleton | page skeleton, top bar keeps its title |
| Empty | first-use copy + action | same, centred |
| Filtered-empty | "No results" + clear | same |
| Error | inline error block with retry, panel stays open | full-page error with retry |
| Streaming / running | persistent step trace + cancel | same, sticky under the top bar |
| Permission denied | explanation + request action | same |
| Disconnected | sidebar footer shows `offline`, banner if actions are blocked | top-bar dot + banner |

---

## 6. Naming conventions in the UI

| Element | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App titles | Title Case | `Task Manager`, `Global Settings` |
| Panel/tab titles | Instance-qualified | `Tasks — Sprint 12`, `File — chat_engine.py` |
| Routes | kebab-case | `/git-view`, `/management-dashboard` |
| Board/column names | user-defined, sentence case | `In progress` |
| Profiles | `snake_case` as identifier, Title Case in prose | `software_developer` |
| Machine values | mono, unchanged | `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `api/chat/chat.py` |

---

## 7. IA checklist for a new app

- [ ] Registered in `config/apps.js` with `id`, `title`, `component`, `icon`, `route`.
- [ ] Added to the correct `MOBILE_APP_GROUPS` group in `config/mobile.js`.
- [ ] Distinct icon from every existing app (check for duplicates — `fa-comments` is
      used twice today).
- [ ] Designed as a **panel** (no own sidebar, no own top bar) **and** as a **route**
      (own title, back affordance, safe-area padding).
- [ ] Multi-instance? Then the title includes the instance and panels do not collide.
- [ ] All seven navigation states above are designed.
- [ ] Deep-linkable if it has internal state (board, chat, team, workspace, file).
